fields.before: Jianwei Han

fields.after: Magistrate of Jujiu

fields.before: Huang led the army in person and captured Xiangping.
fields.after: Huang campaigned against Liaodong in person and captured Xiangping.
fields.sourceReason: Restore Liaodong, the target of the personal campaign (自征遼東).
fields.sourceChinese: 皝自征遼東，克襄平。

fields.before: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed at Juqiu, yielded the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the magistrate and capitulated.
fields.after: Liu Cheng, whom Ren had installed as magistrate of Jujiu, surrendered the town, while Zhang Heng of Xinchang seized the county head and capitulated.
fields.sourceReason: Restore the office 令 and render 居就 as Jujiu in both English fields and repeated uses.

fields.before: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Juqiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
fields.after: Magistrate Liu Cheng of Jujiu, whom Ren had appointed, surrendered the city; a man of Xinchang, Zhang Heng, seized the county chief and surrendered.
fields.sourceReason: Correct the paired-field Juqiu reading; retain the existing explicit magistrate office.
fields.sourceChinese: 仁所署居就令劉程以城降，新昌人張衡執縣宰以降。

fields.before: Troubled by Duan Liao, he sent Song Hui to submit to Shi Hu and beg for an allied expedition.
fields.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly troubled his borders, Huang sent General Song Hui to Shi Hu to declare Huang’s vassalage and request troops to attack Duan Liao.
fields.sourceReason: Restore repeated border trouble, the general title and the specific request for troops; name Huang explicitly to avoid attributing his vassalage to the envoy.
fields.sourceChinese: 皝以段遼屢為邊患，遣將軍宋回稱籓于石季龍，請師討遼。

fields.before: Because Duan Liao repeatedly was a border trouble, sent general Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong, requesting troops to strike Liao.
fields.after: Because Duan Liao repeatedly caused trouble on the frontier, Huang sent General Song Hui to declare vassalage to Shi Jilong and request troops to attack Liao.
fields.sourceReason: The source explicitly makes Huang (皝) the subject, but the existing literal English has no subject before sent. Restore the explicit subject while preserving the general title, repeated frontier trouble, vassalage and troop request.
fields.sourceChinese: 皝以段遼屢為邊患，遣將軍宋回稱籓于石季龍，請師討遼。

fields.before: After a fortnight’s siege his officers begged him to yield.
fields.after: After the two sides held each other off for more than ten days, his attendants urged Huang to surrender.
fields.sourceReason: Render 旬餘 as more than ten days, 左右 as attendants, and make Huang the explicit recipient of their advice.
fields.sourceChinese: 相持旬餘，左右勸皝降。

fields.before: After Duan Liao’s fall Murong Han fled to Yuwen Gui, reckoned his fame would never let him live, and feigned madness—drinking, singing, and disheveled hair.
fields.after: After Duan Liao’s defeat, Murong Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. Believing that his long-established fame and prestige would ultimately endanger his life, he feigned madness, drinking without restraint, letting his hair hang loose, and singing and shouting.
fields.sourceReason: Restore the omitted 建威 title and the long-established fame and prestige; preserve the complete account of feigned madness.
fields.sourceChinese: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。

fields.before: In the beginning, when Duan Liao was defeated, Jianwei Han fled to Yuwen Gui; himself thought his awe-inspiring name long had shaken others, in the end could not preserve whole; thereupon feigned madness, wantonly drank, let hair down and sang and shouted.
fields.after: Earlier, when Duan Liao was defeated, Han, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Yuwen Gui. He thought that, because his fame and prestige had long been renowned, he would not ultimately be able to remain safe; so he feigned madness, drank without restraint, let his hair hang loose, and sang and shouted.
fields.sourceReason: Translate 建威 as an office, rather than leaving Jianwei as an apparent personal name; retain all paired-field propositions.
fields.sourceChinese: 初，段遼之敗也，建威翰奔于宇文歸，自以威名夙振，終不保全，乃陽狂恣酒，被髮歌呼。

fields.before: Huang sent the trader Wang Che to spy; Murong Han met him in silence, only clutching his chest.
fields.after: Huang secretly sent the merchant Wang Che to observe Han; when Han saw Che he said nothing and only stroked his chest.
fields.sourceReason: Restore 陰 and the explicit observation target; render 撫膺 without changing it to clutching.
fields.sourceChinese: 皝遣商人王車陰使察翰，翰見車無言，撫膺而已。

fields.before: He enfeoffed more than a hundred deserving officers.
fields.after: More than a hundred deserving officers were enfeoffed.
fields.sourceReason: Proposed passive rendering preserves the unexpressed Chinese subject without silently choosing Huang as grantor. This does not resolve the held extraction event attribution.
fields.sourceChinese: 封諸功臣百餘人，

fields.before: Enfeoffed the various meritorious ministers over a hundred persons.
fields.after: More than a hundred meritorious officials were enfeoffed.
fields.sourceReason: Preserve the enfeoffment and number without supplying an unexpressed grantor; independently review in the complete imperial-grant context.
fields.sourceChinese: 封諸功臣百餘人，

fields.before: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
fields.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you.
fields.sourceReason: For s0168, explicitly review the documented critical reading: Jinshu jiaozhu says the extant 恨不殺汝 is probably defective for the Tongjian’s 恨恨不欲殺汝; Yulan744 quotes 前燕錄 as 誓不殺汝. Do not treat 恨不 as simply meaning reluctant or silently emend Chinese.
fields.sourceChinese: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。

fields.before: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
fields.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you [the extant text 恨不殺汝 is probably corrupt (晉書斠注): the Tongjian reads 恨恨不欲殺汝, “with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you”; Yulan 744, quoting the 前燕錄, reads 誓不殺汝, “I swear not to kill you”].
fields.sourceReason: The proposed 'am unwilling to kill you' treats 恨不 as if it simply meant 'unwilling', which the scope explicitly rules out. Without any mark it also translates the Tongjian variant in place of the extant 恨不殺汝, which is an emendation made silently in English. The amendment keeps the word-by-word rendering of the extant text, 'I regret not killing you'. It adds the documented critical reading in brackets, citing 晉書斠注's judgment and both witnesses, and changes no Chinese. The first clause takes the proposal's wording, 'a long time'.
fields.sourceChinese: 吾處汝國久，恨不殺汝。

fields.before: That hope dies with me—such is fate.”
fields.after: I never expected that this resolve would go unfulfilled; I die with lingering regret. It is fate. What can be done!”
fields.sourceReason: Restore the unexpected failure of his resolve, his lingering regret at death and the final rhetorical question; preserve the closing quotation.
fields.sourceChinese: 不圖此心不遂，沒有餘恨，命也奈何！」

fields.before: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
fields.after: Orphaned young, with all his brothers also dying early, he stood utterly alone. None even in his clan recognized his worth; only his uncle Dan thought him extraordinary while he was still young, saying, "This child is not only an outstanding talent of our family but also a fine instrument for serving the age."
fields.sourceReason: 雖宗族無能識者 means none of the clan recognized his worth, not merely that few knew him; 幼 refers to Yu when Dan recognized his promise.
fields.sourceChinese: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」

fields.before: In youth orphaned, brothers all died early, alone and solitary; although the lineage group none could recognize him, only uncle Dan in youth wondered at him, saying: “This child is not only our gate’s outstanding show, but an instrument to aid the age.”
fields.after: Orphaned young, with all his brothers dying early, he stood utterly alone. None of the clan recognized his worth; only his uncle Dan, while Yu was still young, thought him extraordinary, saying: “This child is not only our family’s outstanding talent but also a fine instrument for serving the age.”
fields.sourceReason: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. Independently check the explicit subject, quoted idiom, complete objects and contrasts against the supplied Chinese; reject any merely stylistic change.
fields.sourceChinese: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」

fields.before: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
fields.after: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius welcomed Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a bottle gourd; Yi Yin also said, 'Whom may I not serve as ruler? What people may I not command?' If even sages and worthies acted thus, how much more should we!
fields.sourceReason: The proposal rightly corrects the first clause, 何事非君, to 'Whom may I not serve as ruler?'. But it renders 何使非民 as 'Whose people may I not serve?', which is a definite misreading. In Mencius (萬章下 and 公孫丑上), 使 is Yi Yin employing or commanding the people: Zhu Xi glosses it 所使者無非民, and Legge translates 'What people may I not command?'. Serving is the role of the first clause; the second is about directing the people. The amendment changes only that clause and keeps the rest of the proposal word for word, including 匏瓜 (bottle gourd), 聖賢 (sages and worthies) and 況吾曹乎 (how much more our sort).
fields.sourceChinese: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！

fields.before: Yu told friend Cheng Pan, saying: “Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi’s summons, used the gourd as metaphor; Yi Yin also said what affair is not lord, what people not subjects—even sages were thus; how much more our sort!
fields.after: Yu told his friend Cheng Pan: “Confucius welcomed Bi Xi’s summons and used the bottle gourd as a metaphor for himself; Yi Yin also said, ‘Whom may I not serve as ruler? What people may I not command?’ If even sages and worthies were like this, how much more our sort!
fields.sourceReason: The proposal rightly corrects the first clause, 何事非君, to 'Whom may I not serve as ruler?'. But it renders 何使非民 as 'Whose people may I not serve?', which is a definite misreading. In Mencius (萬章下 and 公孫丑上), 使 is Yi Yin employing or commanding the people: Zhu Xi glosses it 所使者無非民, and Legge translates 'What people may I not command?'. Serving is the role of the first clause; the second is about directing the people. The amendment changes only that clause and keeps the rest of the proposal word for word, including 匏瓜 (bottle gourd), 聖賢 (sages and worthies) and 況吾曹乎 (how much more our sort).
fields.sourceChinese: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！

fields.before: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
fields.after: You follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Confucius; surely your insight into the first signs of change is also extraordinary.”
fields.sourceReason: 知機其神 concerns discerning incipient opportunities or changes; Heaven calling is not in this Chinese unit. This repeated Yi/Confucius use is reviewed independently of s0193.
fields.sourceChinese: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」

fields.before: You trace Yi and Kong, or also know the moment’s spirit.”
fields.after: You follow in the tracks of Yi Yin and Confucius; perhaps your discernment of incipient change is truly wondrous.”
fields.sourceReason: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. Independently check the explicit subject, quoted idiom, complete objects and contrasts against the supplied Chinese; reject any merely stylistic change.
fields.sourceChinese: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」

fields.before: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—both he pre-planned their strategies; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
fields.after: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—in both he took part in the planning; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
fields.sourceReason: In 皆豫其謀, 豫 stands for 與 and means to take part in. Yu took part in the planning of both campaigns. 'Pre-planned their strategies' misreads 豫 as 'beforehand'. The idiomatic field already says 'He helped plan' correctly, so only that clause in the literal field changes.
fields.sourceChinese: 東破高句麗，北滅宇文歸，皆豫其謀，皝甚器重之。

fields.before: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.
fields.after: When the capital was moved to Helong, Yang Yu, who had long possessed an ingenious mind, drew up the plans for all the city walls, moats, palaces and gates that Murong Huang built.
fields.sourceReason: 城池宮闔 includes moats and the palace/gate complex; wall and tower alone omits these objects and does not express 皆裕之規模 as Yu’s plans.
fields.sourceChinese: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。

fields.before: When moved the capital to Helong, Yu by nature had clever thought; the city walls and palace towers Huang regulated were all Yu’s models.
fields.after: When the capital was moved to Helong, Yu had long possessed an ingenious mind; the city walls, moats, palaces and gates that Huang built were all planned by Yu.
fields.sourceReason: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. Independently check the explicit subject, quoted idiom, complete objects and contrasts against the supplied Chinese; reject any merely stylistic change.
fields.sourceChinese: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。

fields.before: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
fields.after: Although Yang Yu had served Murong Huang for only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble, respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading posts at court, he lived like a scholar in plain clothes.
fields.sourceReason: 仕皝日近 means his service under Huang was recent or short, not that he grew daily closer to Huang. The complete unit retains the contrast in rank and his personal qualities.
fields.sourceChinese: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。

fields.before: Although Yu served Huang daily nearer, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.
fields.after: Although Yu had served Huang only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble and respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading court posts, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
fields.sourceReason: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. Independently check the explicit subject, quoted idiom, complete objects and contrasts against the supplied Chinese; reject any merely stylistic change.
fields.sourceChinese: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。

fields.before: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.
fields.after: For displaced and isolated gentlemen who died, he invariably arranged their collection and burial, cared for the orphans and bereaved they left, and devoted himself to receiving gentlemen, worthy or unworthy alike; thus he was esteemed wherever he went.
fields.sourceReason: 經營收葬 and 存恤孤遺 distinguish burial arrangements from care for survivors; 士無賢不肖皆傾身待之 explicitly includes worthy and unworthy, a distinction omitted by the current English.
fields.sourceChinese: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。

fields.before: Grandees and scholars who fled in exile and were cut off—none he did not arrange burial for, preserve and pity orphans left behind; gentry whether worthy or not all he inclined his person to treat; therefore wherever he was was pushed and looked up to.
fields.after: For grandees and scholars displaced and cut off from support, he invariably arranged their burial and cared for the orphans and bereaved they left. He devoted himself to receiving scholars, worthy or unworthy alike; thus wherever he was he was esteemed.
fields.sourceReason: Paired-field source review: preserve every proposition while correcting the same mistaken reading or omission as the idiomatic proposal. Independently check the explicit subject, quoted idiom, complete objects and contrasts against the supplied Chinese; reject any merely stylistic change.
fields.sourceChinese: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。

fields.before: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
fields.after: Matters came to the point that the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, suddenly passed away.
fields.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.
fields.sourceChinese: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。

fields.before: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
fields.after: It came to this: the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.
fields.sourceReason: Proposed retrospective rendering of the outcome of the Su Jun/Zu Yue crisis; avoid presenting the dowager’s death as a fresh event during this later memorial. Independently check the interpretation of 至今 against the complete memorial and dated source witness before approval.
fields.sourceChinese: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。

correction.after: East defeated Goguryeo, north destroyed Yuwen Gui—in both he took part in the planning; Huang greatly prized and employed him.
correction.sourceReason: In 皆豫其謀, 豫 stands for 與 and means to take part in. Yu took part in the planning of both campaigns. 'Pre-planned their strategies' misreads 豫 as 'beforehand'. The idiomatic field already says 'He helped plan' correctly, so only that clause in the literal field changes.

correction.before: Although Yu served Huang daily nearer, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.
correction.after: Although Yu’s days serving Huang were recent, favor and rank above the old men’s, nature humble and respectful, clear and frugal, firm, simple, kind, and earnest; although passed through dwelling at court’s apex, like a scholar in plain cloth.
correction.sourceReason: In 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右, 日近 means his days in Huang's service were recent, that is, he had served only a short time. 雖 sets this against 寵秩在舊人之右: although a newcomer, his favor and rank were above the old retainers (舊人). 'Served Huang daily nearer' and 'grew daily closer' misread 日近 as growing closeness and lose the contrast with 舊人. Only that clause changes; the rest of the sentence is kept word for word.
